Finding 2: CPU Usage
Impact is 21.44 active sessions, 17.33% of total activity.
----------------------------------------------------------
Host CPU was a bottleneck and the instance was consuming 84% of the host CPU.
All wait times will be inflated by wait for CPU.
Host CPU consumption was 84%.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 58.11 active sessions, 46.96% of total activity.
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look at the "Top SQL Statements" finding for SQL statements consuming
      significant time on CPU. For example, the SELECT statement with SQL_ID
      "43fh6zrqhuskz" is responsible for 7% of CPU usage during the analysis
      period.

   Recommendation 2: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 21.44 active sessions, 17.33% of total activity.
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider adding more CPUs to the host or adding instances serving the
      database on other hosts.
   Action
      Session CPU consumption was throttled by the Oracle Resource Manager.
      Consider revising the resource plan that was active during the analysis
      period.


Finding 3: Buffer Busy - Hot Objects

----------------------------------------------------------
Read and write contention on database blocks was consuming significant
database time.

Finding 4: Commits and Rollbacks
Impact is 17.69 active sessions, 14.3% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Waits on event "log file sync" while performing COMMIT and ROLLBACK operations
were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Host Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 17.69 active sessions, 14.3% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the possibility of improving the performance of I/O to the
      online redo log files.
   Rationale
      The average size of writes to the online redo log files was 154 K and
      the average time per write was 4 milliseconds.
   Rationale
      The total I/O throughput on redo log files was 37 M per second for reads
      and 70 M per second for writes.
   Rationale
      The redo log I/O throughput was divided as follows: 0% by RMAN and
      recovery, 65% by Log Writer, 0% by Archiver, 0% by Streams AQ and 34% by
      all other activity.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Commit" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 17.69 active sessions, 14.3% of total activity.

         SQL statement with SQL_ID 2qj2nnd7dd4hq.
         declare     owner_lockhandle  VARCHAR2(128);     result INT; begin
         DBMS_LOCK.ALLOCATE_UNIQUE(             lockname => :1 ,
         lockhandle => owner_lockhandle);     result := DBMS_LOCK.REQUEST(
         lockhandle => owner_lockhandle,             lockmode =>
         DBMS_LOCK.SSX_MODE,             timeout => 2,
         release_on_commit => TRUE);     CASE result         WHEN 0 THEN null;
         WHEN 2 THEN RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20000, 'deadlock detected');
         WHEN 4 THEN RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20000, 'lock already obtained');
         ELSE RAISE_APPLICATION_ERROR(-20000, 'request lock failed: ' ||
         result);         END CASE;end;


Finding 2: Buffer Busy - Hot Objects
Impact is 26.44 active sessions, 29.05% of total activity.
----------------------------------------------------------
Read and write contention on database blocks was consuming significant
database time.

   Recommendation 1: Schema Changes
   Estimated benefit is 4.19 active sessions, 4.61% of total activity.

      management in a locally managed tablespace for the tablespace "SYSTEM"
      containing the TABLE "SYS.CCOL$" with object ID 32. Alternatively, you
      can move this object to a different tablespace that is locally managed
      with automatic segment space management.

Finding 3: Log File Switches
Impact is 17.52 active sessions, 19.25% of total activity.
----------------------------------------------------------
Log file switch operations were consuming significant database time while
waiting for checkpoint completion.
This problem can be caused by use of hot backup mode on tablespaces.  DML to
tablespaces in hot backup mode causes generation of additional redo.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 17.53 active sessions, 19.25% of total activity.
   ---------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Verify whether incremental shipping was used for standby databases.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Wait class "Configuration" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is 21.78 active sessions, 23.92% of total activity.


Finding 4: "User I/O" wait Class
Impact is 9.45 active sessions, 10.39% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
Waits for I/O to temporary tablespaces were not consuming significant database
time.
The throughput of the I/O subsystem was not significantly lower than expected.

   No recommendations are available.
